components.description: Shared perturbation-kernel view yields a spectral alignment regularizer for diffusion, with duality to score distillation and empirical gains

nodes.name: REPA needs external encoders
nodes.description: REPA aligns diffusion hidden states with pretrained encoders such as DINOv2 to speed convergence, but depends on foundation-model representations that are often unavailable for modalities like point clouds or graphs.

nodes.name: Diffusion and spectral SRL share perturbation kernels
nodes.description: Diffusion models and self-supervised spectral representation learning can both be formulated under a shared stochastic-process parameterization based on perturbation kernels (Sec 3.1-3.2).

nodes.name: Spectral embeddings preserve neighborhood geometry
nodes.description: Spectral representations built from the diffusion perturbation kernel give time-dependent multi-scale embeddings whose distances reflect local connectivity: small t separates data, large t collapses distances; the diffusion distance expands in the eigenspace of the kernel operator (Prop 4.2).

nodes.name: Spectral alignment regularizer
nodes.description: Diffusion training adds a spectral self-supervised loss L = L_diff + lambda L_s, aligning hidden states with eigenfunctions of a time-varying kernel operator, reusing the same perturbed input plus one additional perturbed view (Sec 4.2, Eq 22).

nodes.name: Spectral objective equals score distillation
nodes.description: Minimizing the spectral self-supervised objective is gradient-equivalent to minimizing a KL divergence, i.e. diffusion score distillation, inducing mode-seeking dynamics in representation space (Prop 4.3, Sec 4.3).

nodes.name: Cleaner synthetic samples
nodes.description: On synthetic 2D distributions (2spirals, rings) the method produces cleaner, more compact samples with fewer outliers than the baseline (Fig 2).

nodes.name: Consistent FID gains on images
nodes.description: Spectral regularization reduces FID by 1.5 on ImageNet-64 (DiT-L/4), 0.2 on ImageNet-256 (DiT-XL/2), 2.8 on CIFAR-10, 3.1 on CelebA and 0.7 on FFHQ, i.e. 15%, 8%, 25%, 11% and 5% relative (Table 1).

nodes.name: Gains persist later in training
nodes.description: The method outperforms the baseline in later stages of training as shown by FID against iterations (Fig 3).

nodes.name: Works for point clouds without encoders
nodes.description: On ShapeNet Chair, Airplane and Car with DiT-3D S/4, where pretrained encoders are unavailable, the method gives strong performance over the baseline (Table 2).

nodes.name: REPA still best for large latent ImageNet-256
nodes.description: For latent-space ImageNet-256, REPA achieves the best overall performance, while the proposed method improves over its baseline without an external pretrained encoder.

nodes.name: Training overhead
nodes.description: Training time increases by about 10% for ImageNet-64 pixel diffusion, 70% for ImageNet-256 latent diffusion and 20% for Airplane point-cloud diffusion.

structural_reasoning: Kernel-based unification motivates a spectral alignment regularizer, supported by duality theory and experiments.
